; 7400 — quad 2-input NAND gate. Derived from the function table
; (datasheet Table 3): each output nY is LOW only when both of that gate's
; inputs are HIGH, and HIGH otherwise.
;
; This is a subunit (multi-gate) package: the four gates are independent,
; so the behavior is one sum-of-products equation per unit, each using that
; unit's own pin names. (renderas: nand fixes the drawn symbol; these
; equations are the authoritative logic.)
;
; Equations are physical-level GALasm: '/' is the complement operator and
; signal names are this file's pin names with any active-low '/' prefix
; dropped (no input here is active-low). Outputs are active-high, so NAND
; is written at the output's declared polarity using De Morgan:
; nY = /nA + /nB ("nY is HIGH when nA is LOW or nB is LOW").
1Y = /1A + /1B
2Y = /2A + /2B
3Y = /3A + /3B
4Y = /4A + /4B
typeData.description: Quad 2-input NAND gate

typeData.behavior:
; 74F381 — 4-bit ALU, A0/B0/F0 = LSB. Combinational (no clock).
;
; Physical-level GALasm: '/' is the complement operator and a signal name is
; this file's pin name (all pins active-high here, so no '/' prefixes). ':+:'
; is the extended-dialect XOR operator (FR-079a); this part models a 74-series
; chip, so it declares no `gal:` and uses the extended dialect.
;
; Function select (S0 S1 S2), from the datasheet Function Select Table:
;   L L L  Clear   (F = 0000)
;   H L L  B minus A     (B + /A + Cn)
;   L H L  A minus B     (A + /B + Cn)
;   H H L  A plus B      (A + B + Cn)
;   L L H  A XOR B
;   H L H  A OR B
;   L H H  A AND B
;   H H H  Preset  (F = 1111)
; The two subtract modes need Cn=1 (a forced carry) to make a true 2's-complement
; difference, per the datasheet note.
;
; Each output bit is written  Fn = <half-sum SOP> :+: <carry-in SOP>  so the
; mode-selected half-sum stays a tiny sum-of-products and only the ripple carry
; grows (cf. 74283). The half-sum is Xn XOR Yn for add/xor, its complement for
; the subtracts (Xn XOR /Yn), An+Bn for OR, An*Bn for AND, 1 for preset, and 0
; for clear; the carry-in term is gated to the three arithmetic modes only, so
; it is 0 (and Fn = half-sum) in the logic/clear/preset modes. Cout is the
; bit-4 carry of the selected arithmetic operation and 0 in the non-arithmetic
; modes (this variant's ripple-carry output; the real 74F381 has /G and /P
; instead). Equations were machine-generated and verified against the ALU
; reference for all 4096 (A, B, S0..S2, Cn) input combinations.
;
; Ovfl (this variant's second added output, on /G's pin) is the signed
; overflow of the selected arithmetic operation, written as the sign rule
; itself: the two effective operand sign bits agree and the result's sign
; disagrees with them. "Effective" because the subtracts feed the adder a
; complemented operand — the MSB pair is (A3, B3) for A plus B, (A3, /B3) for
; A minus B, and (B3, /A3) for B minus A — so each arithmetic mode contributes
; exactly two products: signs both 1 with F3 = 0, and signs both 0 with F3 = 1.
; Six products in all, and the /S2 gating of each one is what makes Ovfl read 0
; in the clear/logic/preset modes rather than undefined.
;
; This reads F3 — one of this part's own combinational outputs — back as an
; input, which is what lets the flag be stated in six terms instead of
; restating the whole carry chain. (The equivalent carry form, C4 XOR C3, is
; the Cout sum XORed with the :+: group of F3: correct, but 138 products and
; unreadable. That was the original spelling; this supersedes it.) Two
; consequences of the feedback are worth knowing: Ovfl settles one unit later
; than F3 under the unit-delay model (FR-078) — invisible in practice, since
; both engines step to quiescence before anything samples — and Ovfl follows
; F3's *net*, so an externally driven or conflicted F3 carries into the flag.
; Verified 4096/4096 against a signed-arithmetic reference (128 genuine
; overflow cases in each arithmetic mode) and against the superseded carry
; form, including with F3 left unconnected.
;
; In a ripple cascade only the most significant slice's Ovfl is meaningful;

; Physical-level GALasm: '/' is the complement operator and a signal name is
; this file's pin name (all pins active-high here, so no '/' prefixes). ':+:'
; is the extended-dialect XOR operator (FR-079a); this part models a 74-series
; chip, so it declares no `gal:` and uses the extended dialect.
;
; Function select (S0 S1 S2), from the datasheet Function Select Table:
;   L L L  Clear   (F = 0000)
;   H L L  B minus A     (B + /A + Cn)
;   L H L  A minus B     (A + /B + Cn)
;   H H L  A plus B      (A + B + Cn)
;   L L H  A XOR B
;   H L H  A OR B
;   L H H  A AND B
;   H H H  Preset  (F = 1111)
; The two subtract modes need Cn=1 (a forced carry) to make a true 2's-complement
; difference, per the datasheet note.
;
; Each output bit is written  Fn = <half-sum SOP> :+: <carry-in SOP>  so the
; mode-selected half-sum stays a tiny sum-of-products and only the ripple carry
; grows (cf. 74283). The half-sum is Xn XOR Yn for add/xor, its complement for
; the subtracts (Xn XOR /Yn), An+Bn for OR, An*Bn for AND, 1 for preset, and 0
; for clear; the carry-in term is gated to the three arithmetic modes only, so
; it is 0 (and Fn = half-sum) in the logic/clear/preset modes. Cout is the
; bit-4 carry of the selected arithmetic operation and 0 in the non-arithmetic
; modes (this variant's ripple-carry output; the real 74F381 has /G and /P
; instead). Equations were machine-generated and verified against the ALU
; reference for all 4096 (A, B, S0..S2, Cn) input combinations.
;
; Ovfl (this variant's second added output, on /G's pin) is the signed
; overflow of the selected arithmetic operation, written as the sign rule
; itself: the two effective operand sign bits agree and the result's sign
; disagrees with them. "Effective" because the subtracts feed the adder a
; complemented operand — the MSB pair is (A3, B3) for A plus B, (A3, /B3) for
; A minus B, and (B3, /A3) for B minus A — so each arithmetic mode contributes
; exactly two products: signs both 1 with F3 = 0, and signs both 0 with F3 = 1.
; Six products in all, and the /S2 gating of each one is what makes Ovfl read 0
; in the clear/logic/preset modes rather than undefined.

; input, which is what lets the flag be stated in six terms instead of
; restating the whole carry chain. (The equivalent carry form, C4 XOR C3, is
; the Cout sum XORed with the :+: group of F3: correct, but 138 products and
; unreadable. That was the original spelling; this supersedes it.) Two
; consequences of the feedback are worth knowing: Ovfl settles one unit later
; than F3 under the unit-delay model (FR-078) — invisible in practice, since
; both engines step to quiescence before anything samples — and Ovfl follows

; 74F381 — 4-bit ALU, A0/B0/F0 = LSB. Combinational (no clock).
;
; Physical-level GALasm: '/' is the complement operator and a signal name is
; this file's pin name (all pins active-high here, so no '/' prefixes). ':+:'
; is the extended-dialect XOR operator (FR-079a); this part models a 74-series
; chip, so it declares no `gal:` and uses the extended dialect.
;
; Function select (S0 S1 S2), from the datasheet Function Select Table:
;   L L L  Clear   (F = 0000)
;   H L L  B minus A     (B + /A + Cn)
;   L H L  A minus B     (A + /B + Cn)
;   H H L  A plus B      (A + B + Cn)
;   L L H  A XOR B
;   H L H  A OR B
;   L H H  A AND B
;   H H H  Preset  (F = 1111)
; The two subtract modes need Cn=1 (a forced carry) to make a true 2's-complement
; difference, per the datasheet note.
;
; Each output bit is written  Fn = <half-sum SOP> :+: <carry-in SOP>  so the
; mode-selected half-sum stays a tiny sum-of-products and only the ripple carry
; grows (cf. 74283). The half-sum is Xn XOR Yn for add/xor, its complement for
; the subtracts (Xn XOR /Yn), An+Bn for OR, An*Bn for AND, 1 for preset, and 0
; for clear; the carry-in term is gated to the three arithmetic modes only, so
; it is 0 (and Fn = half-sum) in the logic/clear/preset modes. Cout is the
; bit-4 carry of the selected arithmetic operation and 0 in the non-arithmetic
; modes (this variant's ripple-carry output; the real 74F381 has /G and /P
; instead). Equations were machine-generated and verified against the ALU
; reference for all 4096 (A, B, S0..S2, Cn) input combinations.
;
; Ovfl (this variant's second added output, on /G's pin) is the signed
; overflow of the selected arithmetic operation, written as the sign rule
; itself: the two effective operand sign bits agree and the result's sign
; disagrees with them. "Effective" because the subtracts feed the adder a
; complemented operand — the MSB pair is (A3, B3) for A plus B, (A3, /B3) for
; A minus B, and (B3, /A3) for B minus A — so each arithmetic mode contributes
; exactly two products: signs both 1 with F3 = 0, and signs both 0 with F3 = 1.
; Six products in all, and the /S2 gating of each one is what makes Ovfl read 0
; in the clear/logic/preset modes rather than undefined.

; input, which is what lets the flag be stated in six terms instead of
; restating the whole carry chain. (The equivalent carry form, C4 XOR C3, is
; the Cout sum XORed with the :+: group of F3: correct, but 138 products and
; unreadable. That was the original spelling; this supersedes it.) Two
; consequences of the feedback are worth knowing: Ovfl settles one unit later
; than F3 under the unit-delay model (FR-078) — invisible in practice, since
; both engines step to quiescence before anything samples — and Ovfl follows

; overflow cases in each arithmetic mode) and against the superseded carry

; the lower slices assert their own and the design must ignore them.

; 74F381 — 4-bit ALU, A0/B0/F0 = LSB. Combinational (no clock).
;
; Physical-level GALasm: '/' is the complement operator and a signal name is
; this file's pin name (all pins active-high here, so no '/' prefixes). ':+:'
; is the extended-dialect XOR operator (FR-079a); this part models a 74-series
; chip, so it declares no `gal:` and uses the extended dialect.
;
; Function select (S0 S1 S2), from the datasheet Function Select Table:
;   L L L  Clear   (F = 0000)
;   H L L  B minus A     (B + /A + Cn)
;   L H L  A minus B     (A + /B + Cn)
;   H H L  A plus B      (A + B + Cn)
;   L L H  A XOR B
;   H L H  A OR B
;   L H H  A AND B
;   H H H  Preset  (F = 1111)
; The two subtract modes need Cn=1 (a forced carry) to make a true 2's-complement
; difference, per the datasheet note.
;
; Each output bit is written  Fn = <half-sum SOP> :+: <carry-in SOP>  so the
; mode-selected half-sum stays a tiny sum-of-products and only the ripple carry
; grows (cf. 74283). The half-sum is Xn XOR Yn for add/xor, its complement for
; the subtracts (Xn XOR /Yn), An+Bn for OR, An*Bn for AND, 1 for preset, and 0
; for clear; the carry-in term is gated to the three arithmetic modes only, so
; it is 0 (and Fn = half-sum) in the logic/clear/preset modes. Cout is the
; bit-4 carry of the selected arithmetic operation and 0 in the non-arithmetic
; modes (this variant's ripple-carry output; the real 74F381 has /G and /P
; instead). Equations were machine-generated and verified against the ALU
; reference for all 4096 (A, B, S0..S2, Cn) input combinations.
;
; Ovfl (this variant's second added output, on /G's pin) is the signed
; overflow of the selected arithmetic operation, written as the sign rule
; itself: the two effective operand sign bits agree and the result's sign
; disagrees with them. "Effective" because the subtracts feed the adder a
; complemented operand — the MSB pair is (A3, B3) for A plus B, (A3, /B3) for
; A minus B, and (B3, /A3) for B minus A — so each arithmetic mode contributes
; exactly two products: signs both 1 with F3 = 0, and signs both 0 with F3 = 1.
; Six products in all, and the /S2 gating of each one is what makes Ovfl read 0
; in the clear/logic/preset modes rather than undefined.

; input, which is what lets the flag be stated in six terms instead of
; restating the whole carry chain. (The equivalent carry form, C4 XOR C3, is
; the Cout sum XORed with the :+: group of F3: correct, but 138 products and
; unreadable. That was the original spelling; this supersedes it.) Two
; consequences of the feedback are worth knowing: Ovfl settles one unit later
; than F3 under the unit-delay model (FR-078) — invisible in practice, since
; both engines step to quiescence before anything samples — and Ovfl follows

; overflow cases in each arithmetic mode) and against the superseded carry
